_comment: License-key extraction rules per software, the asset-management counterpart of cpe-table.json. Each entry: a case-insensitive 'match' regex against the installed-software display name, a human 'label', and 'rules' - one or more of: {type:'registry', path:'HKLM:\...', value:'<name>'}, {type:'file', path:'<file>', regex:'<regex with group 1 = the key>' | jsonfield:'<name>' | line:<n>}, {type:'wmi', class:'<ClassName>', property:'<Prop>', filter:'<WQL filter>'}. Since v5.5.0 three optional extensions exist, all data-only like the rest: 'perUser':true on a registry rule means the path is written 'HKCU:\...' and read from every ALREADY-LOADED user hive (HKEY_USERS\<SID>; hives of logged-off users are never loaded - the extraction stays read-only); 'perUser':true on a file rule allows the placeholder {{profile}} in the path, which becomes each user's profile directory; and exactly ONE '*' per path - in a registry path a whole subkey segment that is enumerated (version-dependent subkeys like 'License.ws.*', at most 20 matches, first non-empty value wins), in a file path a leaf pattern (at most 5 candidate files). At most 20 user profiles are considered per run. Answers carry the user they came from; the first successful read per program wins, and the software CSV's License Source column shows e.g. 'registry (user: alice)'. The script only ever uses these as a registry value / file content / CIM property - never as code. Microsoft keys come from SoftwareLicensingProduct (the 'include Microsoft keys' switch), not from here. Keep the curated set small and correct - ONLY entries with a documented, researched path (cite the source in the pull request); products whose vendors store encrypted blobs are deliberately NOT in this table. Add your own per-program rules in the panel (Software > License keys), they win over every row here.

entries.label: VMware Workstation
entries._source: Broadcom knowledge base 342831 (measured on a fleet install, 2026-11-25): the serial lives in a VERSION-DEPENDENT subkey License.ws.<x>.<y> under the product key, older installs under WOW6432Node - hence the single-segment wildcard, which the v5.5.0 schema can express.

entries.label: Mountain Duck
entries._source: docs.mountainduck.io/mountainduck/installation/ (section 'Registration Key', re-read 2026-11-25 in audit 4): the '*.mountainducklicense' key file is installed in %AppData%\Cyberduck (per user) or C:\ProgramData\Cyberduck (machine-wide) - NOT in a 'Mountain Duck' folder as v5.5.0 assumed (that rule never matched; verified on a Windows 11 install where the file sits in %AppData%\Cyberduck). The file is an XML property list; the registration id is the <string> after <key>Transaction</key>, so the rule extracts that instead of returning the whole signed file.
